chunks: My father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abi al-Jawza' al-Munabbih ibn Abdullah, and Abi al-Khazraj al-Hasan ibn al-Zabarqan, from Fuzayl ibn Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
Take As-Sa'd in your teeth, for it freshens the mouth and increases sexual power.

key_terms.السَّعْد: A plant or material used for brushing teeth, often identified as the toothbrush plant.
key_terms.يُطَيِّبُ الْفَمَ: Freshens the mouth / makes the mouth smell good.

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of using As-Sa'd for teeth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) recommends using *As-Sa'd*—interpreted by Shia scholars as a specific aromatic plant or the miswak—for oral hygiene, linking physical cleanliness with spiritual and marital well-being. The narration highlights the holistic Islamic view where maintaining freshness of the mouth not only pleases God but also enhances intimacy with one's spouse, reflecting the Sunnah of the Prophet and the Imams.
